summary: This is a fragment of a Maven pom.xml file that adds the Mockito library to the project so that tests can create stand-in (mock) objects for interfaces like TemperatureSensor instead of relying on real hardware.

lines.text: The <dependencies> block is where a Maven project lists every external library it needs; Maven downloads each one and puts it on the compile or test classpath for you.
An XML comment marking the spot where the existing JUnit 5 entry sits, so the reader knows Mockito is being added alongside it rather than replacing it.
Each library gets its own <dependency> element, identified by the three coordinates that follow.
The group id names the organisation that publishes the library, much like a package name, and keeps different projects' artifacts from colliding.
The artifact id picks the specific library within that group; mockito-core holds the mocking engine and the familiar mock() and when() methods.
Pinning an exact version means the build behaves the same today and a year from now, instead of silently picking up a newer, possibly incompatible release.
The test scope makes Mockito available to test code only, so the mocking framework is never bundled into the shipped application.
